steps.title: Start the saga
steps.caption: The order starts as PENDING. The orchestrator sends Charge payment; Payments commits and replies ✓.
steps.body: Order Service saves the new order as **PENDING** and starts the saga. The orchestrator records the step in its saga log and sends a *Charge payment* command. Payments charges the card in its own local transaction, commits, and replies with success.

steps.title: Next local transaction
steps.caption: The orchestrator sends Reserve stock; Inventory commits its own local transaction and replies ✓.
steps.body: The orchestrator records the reply and sends the next command, *Reserve stock*. Inventory commits a reservation in its own database and replies. Each step is visible to the rest of the system as soon as it commits: no database lock is held across services while the saga runs.

steps.title: A step fails
steps.caption: Book shipment fails (no courier) and replies ✕. No global rollback: steps 1 and 2 are committed.
steps.body: *Book shipment* fails because no courier is available. Shipping's local transaction rolls back, so nothing is written there, and it replies with a failure. Unlike two-phase commit there is no global rollback: the charge and the reservation are already committed and can only be reversed by new transactions.

steps.title: Compensate in reverse
steps.caption: Compensate in reverse order: Release stock, then Refund payment. The order ends CANCELLED.
steps.body: The orchestrator runs the compensations of the completed steps in reverse order: *Release stock*, then *Refund payment*. Each is a new local transaction with a business meaning (the refund sits next to the charge; nothing is erased). Finally it cancels the order, which ends **CANCELLED**.
